newsitem.title: HUNGARY: BUDAPEST-LISTED FIRMS MAY VIOLATE LAW ON REPORT.
newsitem.headline: BUDAPEST-LISTED FIRMS MAY VIOLATE LAW ON REPORT.

text.p: Some Hungarian bourse listed companies will be in technical violation this year of the law concerning the submission of their audited and approved annual reports for 1996, an adviser to the issuers said.

"These companies violate the law but we believe that the securities law is bad because it did not set any transitional period," Lajos Olah, chairman of the advisory body of bourse issuers, told Reuters.
The problem stems from discrepancy between an old law and a new one.
The Accounting Law allows submission of audited and approved annual report by May 31 the following year, while the new Securities Law brought forward the deadline to April 30.

Hungary's Money and Capital Market Supervision (APTF), the body entitled to enforce the Securities Law, was not available to comment and it was not possible to determine what if any penalties companies that are in violation of the submission requirements might face.
The Securities Law says, however, that companies failing to meet reporting requirements faced a fine of between 50,000 and one million forints.
Olah said companies had prepared late autumn of 1996 their schedule for the audit, the preparation of the balance sheet, the board meetings, the annual general meetings.
Hungary's new Securities Law was passed late last November and has been in effect since January 1, 1997.

The supervision rejected the advisory body's request to treat this as 'case underway', Olah said, adding that a point in the Securities Law says that previous rules are valid for 'cases underway' if the previous rules are more favourable.
Companies which will hold their annual shareholders meetings include oil company MOL and and chemicals TVK .
